title: CAMEL-CLIP: Channel-aware Multimodal Electroencephalography-text Alignment for Generalizable Brain Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2603.13272v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models have shown promise for learning generalizable representations, yet they remain sensitive to channel heterogeneity, such as changes in channel composition or ordering. We propose channel-aware multimodal EEG-text alignment contrastive language image pretraining (CAMEL-CLIP), a contrastive EEG-text multimodal foundation model designed to be robust to heterogeneous channel configurations and widely applicable to diverse downstream tasks. CAMEL-CLIP combines three components: (1) channel attribute-based positional encoding, which identifies channels using their anatomical attributes and reference type; (2) dynamic channel projection, which preserves channel-specific information across varying numbers of EEG channels and combines textual reports with channel information to support channel-wise EEG-text matching; and (3) dual-level contrastive learning, which aligns EEG signals with text

translated_title: CAMEL-CLIP：面向可泛化脑基础模型的通道感知多模态脑电图-文本对齐
translated_abstract: 脑电图（EEG）基础模型在学习可泛化表征方面展现出潜力，但它们对通道异质性（例如通道组成或排序的变化）仍然敏感。我们提出了通道感知多模态脑电图-文本对齐对比语言图像预训练（CAMEL-CLIP），这是一种对比式脑电图-文本多模态基础模型，旨在对异构通道配置具有鲁棒性，并可广泛应用于多种下游任务。CAMEL-CLIP 结合了三个组件：（1）基于通道属性的位置编码，利用通道的解剖属性和参考类型来识别通道；（2）动态通道投影，在不同数量的脑电图通道之间保留通道特定信息，并将文本报告与通道信息相结合以支持逐通道的脑电图-文本匹配；（3）双层对比学习，将脑电信号与文本对齐。
tldr: 提出了通道感知的多模态脑电图-文本对齐基础模型CAMEL-CLIP，通过基于通道属性的位置编码、动态通道投影和双层对比学习，解决了脑电图通道异质性问题，使其能够泛化应用于多种下游任务。
